chapter.title: Memory
chapter.para: Each partition runs in a memory space of its own. The requirements of this chapter state how the spaces are laid out and what the kernel checks when it touches memory of a partition.

section.para: JetOS shall give each partition a memory space of its own: its code and data, its heap and the stacks of its processes, backed by physical memory that no other partition has.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Spatial partitioning is the basis of the isolation of partitions.

section.para: JetOS shall enable the memory protection of the processor (paging on x86_64, the MMU on arm64) before any partition runs.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Without both, a partition could reach the memory of the kernel or of another partition.

section.para: JetOS shall run the partitions in the unprivileged mode of the processor.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Without both, a partition could reach the memory of the kernel or of another partition.

section.para: JetOS shall not let a partition read, write or execute the memory of the kernel or of another partition.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A fault of one partition must stay in that partition.

section.para: JetOS shall handle an attempt of a partition to access memory that is not its own as a memory violation error of the partition (see health monitoring).

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The fault is the partition's, and its health monitoring decides what follows.

section.para: JetOS shall map a configured memory block, by its name, size, virtual address and kind of access (read-only or read-write), into every partition that is allowed to access it, and into no other.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Memory blocks are the way partitions share memory when the configuration says so.

section.para: JetOS shall back a memory block with the same physical memory in all the partitions that it is mapped into.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Memory blocks are the way partitions share memory when the configuration says so.

section.para: JetOS shall give a partition, on request, the address, the size and the access that it has to a memory block named in the request, and an error if it has no such block.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The partition has to find out where a block is mapped.

section.para: JetOS shall check every address that a partition passes to a service.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The kernel must not be made to read or write memory that the partition could not.

section.para: JetOS shall accept an area that a partition passes to a service only if it lies in the code, data and heap of the partition, or in its stacks.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The kernel must not be made to read or write memory that the partition could not.

section.para: A service shall refuse with an error a request of a partition that passes an area outside the code, data, heap and stacks of the partition.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The kernel must not be made to read or write memory that the partition could not.

section.para: A service shall not touch the memory of a request that it refuses for a bad area.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A refused request must leave the partition as it was.

section.para: JetOS shall accept as the entry point of a process only an address in code that the partition can execute.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A process must not start in data or in the memory of another space.

section.para: JetOS shall allocate the stack of each process of a partition from the stack area of the partition, with the size given when the process is created, aligned as the processor requires.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Stacks come from memory that the partition owns, and a restart begins with all of it free.

section.para: JetOS shall give all the stacks of a partition back when the partition restarts.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Stacks come from memory that the partition owns, and a restart begins with all of it free.

section.para: JetOS shall share with each partition an area at the start of its memory, which the kernel and the partition both access, in which they keep the state that the partition's library needs (such as the mode of the partition and the state of its processes and critical sections).

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Some state is cheaper to read in the partition than to ask the kernel for.

section.para: JetOS shall allocate its own memory only while it initializes, from a heap that starts after the kernel image and ends below the memory of the partitions.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: No allocation after the start means no failing allocation and no fragmentation during the operation.

section.para: JetOS shall never free the memory that it has allocated for itself.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: No allocation after the start means no failing allocation and no fragmentation during the operation.

section.para: JetOS shall convert, at the request of a partition, an address of its memory space to the physical address that backs it and back.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The old interface for drivers in partitions that need the physical addresses of their buffers.

section.para: JetOS shall stop the module for a request of a partition to convert an address that does not belong to its memory space.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The old interface for drivers in partitions that need the physical addresses of their buffers.
